items.headline: New MUDA chairman to get State nod for draft Master Plan III on priority
items.gist: Newly nominated MUDA chairman Santhosh Kumar Shetty said on Monday his first priority was getting government approval for the draft Master Plan III for the Mangaluru Local Planning Area, submitted in January and awaiting nod for over seven months; Master Plan II came into effect October 1, 2009, and Plan III should have been in place by 2019. He will discuss it with Urban Development Minister Yatindra Siddaramaiah and District In-charge Minister U.T.
items.paragraph: Newly nominated MUDA chairman Santhosh Kumar Shetty said on Monday his first priority was getting government approval for the draft Master Plan III for the Mangaluru Local Planning Area, submitted in January and awaiting nod for over seven months; Master Plan II came into effect October 1, 2009, and Plan III should have been in place by 2019. He will discuss it with Urban Development Minister Yatindra Siddaramaiah and District In-charge Minister U.T. Khader; once approved, public objections will be invited, and he said MUDA would take up infrastructure beyond MCC jurisdiction in areas such as Surathkal and Bajpe, explore funding for an underpass or flyover, and consider buying private land for parks. Of 200 housing sites on 18 acres at Kunjathbail, 35 have been distributed; 142 sites on 13.5 acres at Konaje are yet to be distributed; work has begun on 700 sites on 45 acres at Chelairu.

items.headline: Man stabs brother to death following fight over mobile phone
items.gist: Adiveppa Kumbara (41), a daily-wage labourer from Belagavi district, was allegedly stabbed in the chest and killed by his younger brother Raju Kumbara near Kottara Cross on Sunday night following a quarrel over a mobile phone, Police Commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy C H said. The brothers, both alcohol-dependent and living with their mother Eravva in a rented house for about a year, had fought after Adiveppa took Raju's phone at their mother's petty shop; Adiveppa was declared dead at Wenlock Hospital after the assault around 10.45 pm.

The brothers, both alcohol-dependent and living with their mother Eravva in a rented house for about a year, had fought after Adiveppa took Raju's phone at their mother's petty shop; Adiveppa was declared dead at Wenlock Hospital after the assault around 10.45 pm. The Urwa Police have arrested Raju and registered a case under section 103(1) of the BNS.

items.headline: INTACH organises Hindustani vocal recital
items.gist: The Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) Mangaluru Chapter and the Art Kanara Trust organised the eighth edition of the Baithak at Kodialguthu in the Musical Heritage of Karnataka series, featuring a Hindustani vocal recital by Neeharika Deraje at the Kodialguthu Centre for Art & Culture, Ballalbagh. Neeharika was accompanied by Shrivathsa Sharma on tabla, Medha G Bhat on harmonium and Samveda G Bhat on tanpura; she opened with Raag Puriya Dhanashree and also presented compositions in Raag Durga.

items.headline: Slew of events to mark 'Alzheimer's Month' celebrations starting today
items.gist: People's Association for Geriatric Empowerment (PAGE) will observe Alzheimer's Month throughout September with memory screening programmes, awareness activities and competitions for senior citizens, launching celebrations at Kadri Park on September 1 at 7 am. Dr Prabha Adhikari, PAGE vice-president, said early diagnosis can delay dementia progression and that India is estimated to have nearly 8.8 million people living with dementia, over 90% undiagnosed; Yenepoya Medical College will conduct free memory, blood pressure and blood sugar tests at Kadri Park on September 1 from 7.30 am to 10 am.
items.paragraph: People's Association for Geriatric Empowerment (PAGE) will observe Alzheimer's Month throughout September with memory screening programmes, awareness activities and competitions for senior citizens, launching celebrations at Kadri Park on September 1 at 7 am. Dr Prabha Adhikari, PAGE vice-president, said early diagnosis can delay dementia progression and that India is estimated to have nearly 8.8 million people living with dementia, over 90% undiagnosed; Yenepoya Medical College will conduct free memory, blood pressure and blood sugar tests at Kadri Park on September 1 from 7.30 am to 10 am. Competitions for seniors will be held at Rotary Club Mangalore North on World Alzheimer's Day, September 21, from 2 pm to 6 pm, with the grand finale at Town Hall.

items.headline: Auto fares hiked in Mangaluru from today
items.gist: Autorickshaw fares will go up in Mangaluru on Tuesday, with the minimum for the first 1.5 km rising from ₹35 to ₹40 and every subsequent kilometre from ₹15 to ₹20, after the RTA headed by Dakshina Kannada Deputy Commissioner H.V. Darshan approved the revision in an order on Friday citing rising costs of fuel, CNG, and spare parts.
items.paragraph: Autorickshaw fares will go up in Mangaluru on Tuesday, with the minimum for the first 1.5 km rising from ₹35 to ₹40 and every subsequent kilometre from ₹15 to ₹20, after the RTA headed by Dakshina Kannada Deputy Commissioner H.V. Darshan approved the revision in an order on Friday citing rising costs of fuel, CNG, and spare parts. There will be no waiting charge for the first 10 minutes and ₹5 for every subsequent 15 minutes; between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. drivers may collect 1.5 times the normal fare, and the revised chart must be displayed with meters recalibrated. Dakshina Kannada is now on a par with Udupi and Shivamogga (₹40 and ₹20 from September 14, 2022 and November 14, 2022); previous DK fares of ₹35 and ₹17 per subsequent km had been in effect since October 27, 2022.

items.headline: Cabinet meeting in Mangaluru on Sept 18
items.gist: The Karnataka government has decided to hold a State Cabinet meeting in Mangaluru on September 18, with proposals concerning the coastal districts likely to receive special priority. Chief Secretary Shalini Rajneesh has directed Additional Chief Secretaries, Principal Secretaries and Secretaries of all government departments to immediately prepare coastal-district proposals and place them before the Cabinet in the form of Cabinet notes.

items.headline: MCC body makes 4-way waste segregation a must
items.gist: The Mangaluru City Corporation has made segregation of waste into wet, dry, sanitary and special-care categories mandatory at source for residents and all bulk waste generators, giving citizens one month to comply before collection staff refuse improperly segregated waste. Wet and sanitary waste will be collected daily, dry and special-care waste on Fridays, and violations will attract penalties under the MCC Solid Waste Management Bye-laws, 2019.

items.headline: Class 9 student ends life for scoring less marks in exam
items.gist: Shravan (14) of Kokkada allegedly died by suicide on Sunday after being upset over scoring three out of 40 marks in Hindi, his uncle Sathish Gowda K told the Dharmasthala Police in a complaint filed on Monday. Shravan's father had attended a parent-teacher meeting at the private school on Saturday, where a teacher informed him of the low score; the boy reportedly locked himself in his study room and was found dead later.

items.headline: Hindu activists allege PFI's involvement in Puttur clash; demand thorough probe
items.gist: The Vishva Hindu Parishad, Bajrang Dal and Hindu Jagarana Vedike, Puttur unit, staged Puttur Chalo on Monday demanding withdrawal of the case registered against the owner of a digital service centre in Darbe and a thorough probe into document-damage incidents. Protesters alleged banned PFI activists were involved in the clash and demanded FIRs against them under the Karnataka Control of Organised Crime Act, action against police for allegedly delaying case registration, and arrest of those who entered a police jeep and obstructed personnel.

items.headline: ICAR–CPCRI to celebrate World Coconut Day tomorrow
items.gist: World Coconut Day 2026 will be celebrated at the ICAR–Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (ICAR–CPCRI), Kasaragod, on September 2, with the theme 'Coconuts in Times of Uncertainty: Securing Food, Energy, and Livelihoods.' ICAR–CPCRI will launch SHITIZ 2.0, an online entrepreneur mentorship and pre-incubation programme, and inaugurate a two-day stakeholders' workshop on management of extreme climate vulnerability in plantation crops. Dr Dinakar Adiga, Director, ICAR–Directorate of Cashew Research, Puttur, will inaugurate the celebrations; outstanding farmers and entrepreneurs will be felicitated and MoUs signed to promote technology commercialisation in the plantation sector.

items.headline: Alva's student gets Rs 46.33-lakh job package
items.gist: Srushti Manjunath Ullagaddi, a final-year Information Science Engineering student at Alva's Institute of Engineering and Technology (AIET), has been selected as a Software Engineer by Visa with annual compensation and quantified benefits totalling Rs 46.33 lakh. Her base annual compensation is Rs 35.58 lakh, with family medical insurance worth Rs 7.5 lakh, OPD benefit of Rs 25,000 and education subsidy up to Rs 3 lakh; a 10-week Visa internship during her sixth semester with a Rs 90,000 stipend led to the full-time offer.

items.headline: Puttur Cong MLA writes to CM, alleges corruption in KRIDL
items.gist: Puttur MLA Ashok Kumar Rai has urged Chief Minister D K Shivakumar to order an investigation into allegations of corruption, illegal collection of money and threats to contractors by officials of the Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited (KRIDL), Mangaluru division, in a letter dated August 25. Rai alleged KRIDL Mangaluru Executive Engineer Vijay and Junior Engineer Prajwal collected additional amounts of up to seven per cent from contractors in the name of a "KRIDL charge" and that contractors were told monthly payments had to be made to the district in-charge and department ministers.

Rai alleged KRIDL Mangaluru Executive Engineer Vijay and Junior Engineer Prajwal collected additional amounts of up to seven per cent from contractors in the name of a "KRIDL charge" and that contractors were told monthly payments had to be made to the district in-charge and department ministers. items.headline: Puttur temple devotees seek probe into alleged irregularities
items.gist: Devotees and citizens of Puttur have petitioned the Karnataka Department of Religious Endowments seeking an inquiry into alleged administrative irregularities, rule violations and controversial developmental works at Sri Mahalingeshwara Temple, including demolition of the Naga Sannidhi, Ayyappa Swamy and Navagraha shrines without prior approval. The complaint also questions the dismantling of a Nataraja platform and a 3,000 sq ft building, the cutting of more than 15 coconut trees, filling of at least seven open wells, and a proposed 30-foot road along the northern side that complainants say could use around four acres of temple property.

items.headline: Hindu organisations seek arrest of group that assaulted photocopy centre owners

items.paragraph: The High Court of Karnataka has quashed acquisition of 1,938 acres for the Karnataka Housing Board’s Suryanagar 4th phase residential layout, holding the land is part of areas proposed as eco-sensitive zone of Bannerghatta National Park and abuts elephant corridors; a Division Bench of Justice D.K. Singh and Justice H. Shanthi Bhushan passed the order on August 29, setting aside a single judge’s January 2025 verdict. The Bench said since the project falls within BNP’s proposed ESZ of 268.96 sq. km., the whole project is misconceived and would have irreversible ecological consequences; KHB began acquisition in 2013 across five Anekal taluk villages — Konasandra, Bommandahalli, Kadujakkanahalli, Indlavadi, and Bagganadoddi. MoEFCC proposed an ESZ of 268.96 sq. km in a 2016 draft, later reduced to 168.84 sq. km in a March 2020 final notification; the CEC’s January 2026 report on a plea by K.B. Belliappa recommended restoring 268.96 sq. km, while MoEFCC said it is studying that recommendation.

items.headline: Rs 72 lakh for 30x40 site: BDA starts accepting applications for Karanth layout
items.gist: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Monday announced allotment of 2,815 sites to the general public in the 3,700-acre Dr K Shivaram Karanth Layout spread over 17 villages in northern Bengaluru, with a 30x40 sq ft site priced at Rs 72 lakh at Rs 6,000 per square foot. The Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) has started accepting applications through the Seva Sindhu portal; the layout comprises 24,714 sites in total, with 18,399 reserved for landowners who parted with land in 2020-21 and the project costing Rs 16,419.89 crore.

items.headline: Independent judiciary vital to protect human rights: ICJ judge
items.gist: An independent and impartial judiciary, coupled with collective global responsibility, is essential to protecting human rights and addressing emerging challenges, International Court of Justice (ICJ) Judge Leonardo Nemer Caldeira Brant said on Monday delivering a special lecture at CMR University's School of Legal Studies in Bengaluru. Judge Brant said the ICJ plays a crucial role in upholding international law and that human rights had evolved into a shared global responsibility requiring independent judicial institutions.
items.paragraph: An independent and impartial judiciary, coupled with collective global responsibility, is essential to protecting human rights and addressing emerging challenges, International Court of Justice (ICJ) Judge Leonardo Nemer Caldeira Brant said on Monday delivering a special lecture at CMR University's School of Legal Studies in Bengaluru. Judge Brant said the ICJ plays a crucial role in upholding international law and that human rights had evolved into a shared global responsibility requiring independent judicial institutions. He underlined the growing importance of international legal mechanisms in dealing with challenges such as climate change and environmental protection, and urged civil society to remain actively engaged in protecting fundamental rights.

items.gist: The National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (Nimhans) on Monday inaugurated its renovated creche for faculty members' children, designed around experiential learning and a child-first approach. items.headline: 18 years after notification, Authority finally allots sites to land-losers
items.gist: For landowners who waited nearly two decades since the Dr Shivaram Karanth Layout was first notified in 2008, the BDA's commencement of site allotment on Monday marks a major milestone after prolonged litigation and Supreme Court intervention in 2018. A committee headed by Justice A V Chandrashekar, formed in December 2020, coordinated land acquisition and layout formation, with civil works split among nine construction firms from December 2022; landowners such as M Devaraj of Kalathammanahalli received six developed sites for about 32 guntas surrendered.

items.headline: Threats against event organisers won't be tolerated: Priyank
items.gist: Home Minister Priyank Kharge on Monday said threats on social media against people organising events would not be tolerated, responding to questions about the Karnataka High Court pulling up Whitefield police over alleged illegal arrests and referring to the station as "Darkfield." Kharge said there had been a communication gap and that the person detained was a repeat offender not connected to comedian Kunal Kamra; Whitefield police had registered a suo motu FIR after Mohan Gowda of the Hindu Rashtra Samanvaya Samiti posted on social media that cancellation of an event was a victory for Hindu unity. In a separate interaction with over 800 police officers, Kharge said the government would stand by honest policemen but not protect those acting against the law.

items.headline: 6-member committees for reverification of guarantee beneficiaries
items.gist: The Karnataka government has constituted six-member committees at panchayat and ward levels for reverification of beneficiaries of the five flagship guarantee schemes, with each committee comprising two women, one SC/ST, one general category, one minority and one OBC member. Guarantee Implementation Authority Chairman H M Revanna said reverification is expected to involve filling forms via an app with phone numbers, photos and addresses; Chief Minister D K Shivakumar held a meeting on Monday where major decisions on reverification were taken.

items.headline: Gruha Jyothi beneficiary survey deadline extended
items.gist: The Karnataka government has extended until September 30 the deadline for the ongoing door-to-door survey of beneficiaries under the Gruha Jyothi scheme, which provides up to 200 units of free electricity to households as one of the Congress government's five guarantee schemes. items.headline: Food safety crackdown on 16 sweet manufacturing units in state; major violations found
items.gist: Food Safety and Drug Administration officials on Monday conducted a special inspection drive at sweet manufacturing units in Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, Greater Bengaluru Authority, Mysuru, Dakshina Kannada, Belagavi, Kalaburagi and Hubballi-Dharwad, collecting samples of sweets, cooking oil, khova, Mysore Pak and other products for laboratory examination. items.gist: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar's Prajaseva citizen connect campaign will start on September 5 from Kudligi hobli in Vijayanagar district, Chief Secretary Shalini Rajneesh said in a statement on Monday. The Prajaseva Abhiyana will be an integrated system for directly hearing citizens' grievances and providing redress on the spot or within a specified timeframe; meetings will be held on the first and third Saturdays at taluk headquarters under district in-charge ministers and on the second and fourth Saturdays at taluk/hobli level under local MLAs.

items.headline: Amid KPSC probe, govt drafts rules for stringent exam law
items.gist: Coinciding with the investigation into alleged scams at the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), the state government has published draft rules to operationalise the Karnataka Public Examination (Measures for Prevention of Corruption and Unfair Means in Recruitment) Act, 2023, notified in September 2024. Those found guilty of unfair means face imprisonment of five to 12 years and fines from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 10 crore; draft rules published by the Home Department on August 24 propose investigations into offences including question paper leaks be completed within three months.

Those found guilty of unfair means face imprisonment of five to 12 years and fines from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 10 crore; draft rules published by the Home Department on August 24 propose investigations into offences including question paper leaks be completed within three months. The rules permit biometric verification, QR code tracking, GPS tracking, CCTV surveillance and AI-based anomaly detection, and bar candidates from carrying mobile phones, smart watches and other prohibited devices unless specifically permitted.

items.headline: KPSC scam: CID arrests middleman who made crores
items.gist: The Criminal Investigation Department has arrested Basavaraj Kannale, a Bhalki-based alleged middleman, in connection with the KPSC veterinary officers recruitment scam, opening a new line of investigation into the suspected network behind alleged recruitment irregularities. Investigators are examining allegations that he used purported political contacts and photographs with leaders of both the BJP and Congress to convince aspirants he had influence over recruitment, and are probing his financial dealings, communications and links with officials including an alleged connection with IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar.

items.headline: ED issues lookout notice against Commission member Shanta Hosamani
items.gist: The Enforcement Directorate (ED), separately probing alleged KPSC irregularities, has issued a lookout notice at airports against KPSC member Shanta Hosamani, who has been untraceable since ED raids on August 18 and has failed to respond to ED notices. items.headline: CM says K'swamy targeting BJP, not Cong on KPSC scam
items.gist: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said JD(S) leader H D Kumaraswamy was targeting the BJP, not the Congress, over the alleged KPSC scam and was free to make whatever allegations he wanted. Shivakumar said he would not interfere in the investigation including arrests of an IAS officer, that the BJP was free to undertake its padayatra from Lingasugur to Ballari from Tuesday, and that a proposed land guarantee initiative would benefit all whose property is acquired for government purposes across the state, not only Bengaluru.

items.headline: Energy dept to accelerate installation of solar rooftop systems on govt bldgs
items.gist: The state government will accelerate installation of Solar Rooftop Photovoltaic (SRTPV) systems on government buildings under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, the energy department said on Monday, noting that though close to 59,000 government buildings have potential for SRTPV, only 2,624 have systems installed. Energy Minister K J George said priority will be given to Deputy Commissioners' offices and other government buildings with adequate rooftop space; under the RESCO model, developers bear the entire project cost and operation and maintenance, while departments can also opt for a CAPEX model with EPC developers selected through bidding.

items.headline: Wild jumbo electrocuted
items.gist: A wild female elephant aged around 35 years died of electrocution at Kogilamane village in Belur taluk of Hassan district on Monday after coming in contact with a live wire under an electricity pole. A herd of wild elephants had strayed into the village in search of food when the jumbo was electrocuted on the spot; forest department officials visited the spot and veterinarian Dr Vinayaka of Bhadra Tiger Reserve conducted the post-mortem.

items.headline: Nursing colleges accused of charging excess fees from students
items.gist: Following the second round of seat allotment for professional courses, the Karnataka Examinations' Authority (KEA) has received complaints that some nursing colleges are charging excess fees beyond the prescribed Rs 10,000 for government quota, Rs 1 lakh for Karnataka management quota and Rs 1.4 lakh for non-Karnataka management quota seats. Some colleges are allegedly demanding an additional Rs 50,000 from government quota students; the Admission Overseeing Committee at Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) and KEA have received numerous complaints.

items.headline: FIR against medical officer for making patients clean hospital cesspit
items.gist: The medical officer of Savanur Taluk Hospital in Haveri district, Dr S Y Hiregowdar, and nursing supervisor Vaneetha were named in an FIR on Monday after two patients were tasked with cleaning the hospital cesspit on August 28. Haveri Deputy Commissioner Vijay Mahantesh Danammanavar directed the tahsildar to register the FIR at Savanur police station after Social Welfare Department officials visited the hospital to ascertain facts; both have been summoned for questioning and the District Health Officer is learnt to have recommended suspending them.

items.headline: Develop dashboard-based online system to lodge plaints: Khandre
items.gist: Rural Development and Panchayat Raj (RDPR) Minister Eshwar Khandre has directed officials to develop a dashboard-based online system for registering and resolving complaints related to gram panchayat services including e-Swathu, property tax, lake encroachments, Jal Jeevan Mission, sanitation and rural roads. Khandre said the RDPR department's direct contact with nearly half the state's population made prompt grievance redress important, and directed his secretary to develop a web portal and application allowing rural residents to register complaints with videos and photographs.

Khandre said the RDPR department's direct contact with nearly half the state's population made prompt grievance redress important, and directed his secretary to develop a web portal and application allowing rural residents to register complaints with videos and photographs. items.headline: 20 lakh hectares unsown as sowing closes for kharif crops
items.gist: As the sowing window for most kharif crops draws to a close, agriculture department data as of August 28 shows 20 lakh hectares of the 84.1 lakh hectare kharif target remained unsown, with cereals alone accounting for 15 lakh uncultivated hectares amid deficit rainfall and adverse weather. Paddy has been sown on only 4.87 lakh hectares against a 10 lakh target, ragi on 4.62 against 8.2 lakh and maize on 13 against 17.3 lakh; Agriculture Minister P M Narendraswamy said good sowing need not mean a good crop and that the department has received over 37 lakh crop insurance applications, an all-time high.

items.headline: BJP to launch 'Ballari Chalo' against Cong 'misrule' today
items.gist: The BJP has prepared for its 175-km padayatra beginning from Lingasugur in Raichur district on Tuesday (September 1), passing through Maski, Sindhanur, Karatagi, Gangavati, Kampli and Kudatini before reaching Ballari in Sandur constituency over 10 days. Senior leaders including Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, BJP state president B Y Vijayendra, LoP R Ashoka and Deputy LoP Arvind Bellad are expected to participate; around 30,000 people are expected at the launch on a 4-acre stage on the Lingasugur bypass and about 700 police personnel have been deputed.

items.headline: Nepal flood survivors recount narrow escape
items.gist: Karnataka tourists caught in Nepal's devastating flash floods recounted a desperate fight for survival, with survivors describing a deafening roar, torrents of water and debris leaving little time to react. Basavaraj Hosamani (52) of Haveri district, part of a group from Rattihalli, said a traffic jam proved their saviour on August 26 when they learned the magnitude of devastation along the Trishuli River route they had photographed just 24 hours earlier; the group of 54 returned to Bengaluru on August 29 by flight after a 13-hour journey to the Sonauli border instead of the usual four hours due to destroyed roads and bridges.

items.headline: ITC Infotech to buy 22.1% stake in Happiest Minds for Rs 1,330 cr
items.gist: Bengaluru-based Happiest Minds will merge with ITC Infotech India Limited, with the latter acquiring an aggregate 22.1% minority stake from promoter Ashok Soota and promoter entities across two tranches for a total consideration of Rs 1,330 crore. The combined entity will be an AI-first global technology services enterprise targeting $1 billion of annual revenue by FY28, with over 19,000 employees and ITC Limited holding a 73.4% stake post-merger under a share swap of 25 ITC Infotech shares for every 81 Happiest Minds shares.

items.gist: Onion prices have surged in Bengaluru amid a rainfall deficit in Karnataka, with retail prices rising from around Rs 15–20 per kg to Rs 40–50 per kg. items.headline: Shikshagraha partners with Teach for India
items.gist: Shikshagraha on Monday announced a partnership with Teach For India, combining the latter's 17 years of experience in nurturing teachers, young leaders and alumni with a movement that has already mobilised more than 3.9 lakh leaders across 2.1 lakh public schools. Shikshagraha, a people's movement working to strengthen one million public schools across India, said Teach For India brings classroom leadership experience while Shikshagraha contributes a network of more than 40 civil society organisations; it cited more than 15.6 lakh micro-improvements across public schools led by over 3.9 lakh leaders reaching more than 2.1 lakh schools.

items.headline: Nepal floods: 2 from Tumakuru go missing
items.gist: Two US citizens originally from Tumakuru—Rangusudheer, 53, and Keerthi Acharya, 50, residents of Nrupatunga Layout—are among those reported missing after devastating floods in Nepal, leaving family members in Karnataka deeply worried. Both software engineers had travelled to Nepal from the US on August 22 as part of a 10-member group; Rangusudheer last spoke to a relative at around 8.29am on August 26, after which the family lost contact with both.

items.headline: CWMA water-release order being enforced: Karnataka
items.gist: Karnataka told the Supreme Court it was complying with the Cauvery Water Management Authority direction to ensure 9,000 cusecs of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, after CWMA on August 25 upheld the CWRC recommendation of 9,000 cusecs for 15 days. Senior advocate Shyam Divan said 9,888 cusecs were released on August 30 and flow had crossed 11,000 cusecs by Monday morning, while Tamil Nadu sought 17.604 tmc ft as the balance due as of August 27 under the pro-rata formula.

items.headline: Three of family run over by train
items.gist: A woman and her two granddaughters — Irfana and granddaughters Rukhiya and Raziya, from Hindupur in Andhra Pradesh — were killed on the spot after being run over by an express train between Doddaballapur and Muttur on Monday morning. The girls had come to their grandmother’s house from Hindupur for the holidays; the family was walking towards Doddaballapur railway station from Muttur when they stepped on the railway track where two tracks meet at a curve and allegedly failed to notice the approaching train.

items.headline: KPSC ‘scam’: Priyank offers to quit politics if there is iota of evidence against him
items.gist: Home Minister Priyank Kharge offered to resign if even an iota of evidence showed his involvement in the alleged KPSC AEE recruitment scam under the Rural Drinking Water Supply Scheme, and challenged Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy to retire if BJP or JD(S) involvement was found.
items.paragraph: Home Minister Priyank Kharge offered to resign if even an iota of evidence showed his involvement in the alleged KPSC AEE recruitment scam under the Rural Drinking Water Supply Scheme, and challenged Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy to retire if BJP or JD(S) involvement was found. Kharge said two FIRs had already been registered, OMR sheets were in KPSC custody, a five-member committee submitted a report a day after RDPR issued conditional appointment orders, and KPSC shared findings only in February this year, blaming the examination wing not the government. Kumaraswamy, speaking in Delhi, said he wanted a transparent probe not Kharge’s retirement and alleged candidates were kept at resorts, question papers provided and OMR sheets manipulated.

items.headline: Q1 GDP grows at 7.8%, defies war impact
items.gist: India's GDP expanded by 7.8% in the first quarter of the current financial year, driven by robust growth in services and manufacturing despite global disruptions from the West Asia conflict, according to official data released on Monday. The April-June growth is slower than the previous quarter's 8.6% expansion but higher than the 6.9% recorded in Q1 of 2025-26.

items.headline: SC: Won't stop Sept 5 CJP march; trust it will be peaceful
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to restrain the Cockroach Janta Party from staging a protest march in Delhi on September 5, with a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana expressing confidence the demonstration would remain peaceful. Advocate Rizwan Ahmed argued the demand was not urgent and cited police raids and international media presence; the bench said counsel could file an application if any untoward incident occurred and directed that the matter be considered by the police, referring broader issues to a High-Powered Committee.

items.headline: 14% monsoon shortfall so far, Sept too will be deficient: IMD
items.gist: Three months into the southwest monsoon season, all southern states remain severely rain deficient with little hope of recovery in September, which is likely to receive below-normal showers, the India Meteorological Department said on Monday, adding that August was the hottest month on record since 1901. Karnataka has a cumulative shortfall of 23%, Andhra Pradesh tops the list at 42%, Kerala and Tamil Nadu are both at 21%, Telangana at 19%, and the national deficiency is 14%, with September rainfall expected at 91% of the 167.9 mm average.

items.headline: Minor girl gang-raped on moving bus in Noida
items.gist: Police said a 17-year-old Class 11 student from Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh, was allegedly gang-raped by sleeper-bus driver Kuldeep and conductor Sandeep around 11.30 p.m. on August 4 during a journey from Pari Chowk in Greater Noida toward Sector 63 and then Outer Ring Road, after they offered her a lift; both have been arrested and the bus seized for forensic examination.

items.headline: Externment order can't be passed routinely, says Supreme Court
items.gist: The Supreme Court held that an externment order directly impinges on fundamental freedoms and cannot be passed as a matter of routine, and that multiple criminal cases alone do not justify externment. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said the District Magistrate must have bona fide subjective satisfaction with objective material and a discernible nexus before issuing such an order.
items.paragraph: The Supreme Court held that an externment order directly impinges on fundamental freedoms and cannot be passed as a matter of routine, and that multiple criminal cases alone do not justify externment. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said the District Magistrate must have bona fide subjective satisfaction with objective material and a discernible nexus before issuing such an order. The court quashed the November 4, 2025 externment order against Vijay Kumar Rajpoot alias Viju by the Raigarh District Magistrate and faulted the Chhattisgarh High Court for a hands-off approach, allowing him to return to the districts from which he had been externed.

items.headline: Indus water pact in force, rules Hague court; India rejects
items.gist: A World Bank-constituted court of arbitration ruled on Monday that the more than six-decade-old Indus Water Treaty between India and Pakistan remains fully in force despite New Delhi putting it in abeyance after the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 Indian citizens. India rejected the Hague-based award as an illegally constituted body with no jurisdiction over sovereign decisions, while the tribunal unanimously found no grounds for suspension or termination and barred India from concreting the dam wall and power intake of the 850-MW Ralte Hydroelectric Plant on the Chenab beyond certain levels until 90 days after the Neutral Expert's final decision, expected in July 2027.

items.headline: India is 'vishwa guru', not a superpower: RSS chief Bhagwat
items.gist: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said India's civilisational traditions have always guided the principle of helping others without discrimination, and that the country has served the world as a 'vishwa guru' and not as a 'superpower'. Addressing the 'Hindu Vishwa Bandhu – Embrace the World in Friendship' event organised by Canadian Hindus for Outreach, Relations and Dialogue in Toronto on Sunday, he said the Hindu worldview was universal, rooted in 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam', and that Bharat extends help even without being asked.

items.headline: SC: Real victim can settle for quashing criminal cases
items.gist: The Supreme Court ruled that the real victim of a crime—not necessarily the informant or complainant—is authorised to enter into a settlement that can form the basis for quashing criminal proceedings under the High Court's Section 482 inherent power, while compounding under Section 320 CrPC (now Section 359 BNSS) remains strictly statutory. A bench of Justices K V Vishwanathan and Arun Palli drew the distinction while hearing an appeal by Anand Kumar alias Sanjay Lalwani against a Madhya Pradesh High Court order refusing to quash a 2018 criminal case because the informant was not party to the compromise.

items.headline: With just Rs 3 in account, Rs 4-cr cheque to Ram Temple returned
items.gist: A Chennai woman's cheque of Rs 4.1 crore donated to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya was returned after the bank reportedly found her account balance was just Rs 3; the Coimbatore resident had also donated Rs 10,000 in cash. Reports said she issued the cheque to increase wages of temple trust employees but asked for a written assurance on use of funds, which the trust did not oblige; the 2020 donation campaign raised Rs 3,500 crore, with cheques worth Rs 100 crore later returned on technical grounds.

items.headline: Fadnavis dubs CJP 'Congress Jitao Programme'
items.gist: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Monday dubbed the Cockroach Janta Party as "Congress Jitao Programme" and accused the Opposition of forcing political contests over isolated issues after failing to defeat the BJP ideologically, also terming Rahul Gandhi's "Chhatron Ki Goonj" outreach as "Jhooth Ki Goonj." Addressing the BJP's state-level convention in Pune, Fadnavis said the Opposition had taken up issues including Ayodhya Ram Temple donation theft and Zilla Parishad school conditions, and commented on the Pune debate over loudspeakers during Ganeshotsav.

items.headline: Over 6 crore names deleted so far in third phase of SIR
items.gist: As the third phase of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in 16 States and three Union Territories nears its end, more than 6 crore names have been deleted as per draft lists: of 36.08 crore names, 29.93 crore have been retained and 6.15 crore, or 17.04%, removed, though final numbers could differ after claims and objections; drafts are out except Nagaland (September 20) and Tripura (October 21), with Delhi and Maharashtra published on Monday. Delhi has the highest deletions in percentage terms at 32.78%; Maharashtra saw the most names removed at 2.06 crore, followed by Karnataka at 1.07 crore, then Telangana 73,39,235, Andhra Pradesh 44,89,512, Jharkhand 43,61,987, Haryana 33.83 lakh, Punjab 20,66,635, and Odisha 20,12,557.

Final rolls start September 6 with Mizoram, Sikkim and Manipur first; Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar wrote to CEC Gyanesh Kumar calling the deletions “massive and unjustified” and urging an extension of the claims window, and the Telangana Chief Minister has done the same.

items.headline: In firepower boost, Tatas to make US Javelin missiles in India
items.gist: Tata Advanced Systems on Monday signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Javelin Joint Venture of Lockheed Martin and Raytheon as the "prime partner" for commercial production of Javelin anti-tank guided missiles in India, days after India and the US inked a $45-million government-to-government contract to purchase 100 Javelin systems. The firms will explore a final assembly and integration facility in India; sub-assembly kits and guidance electronics will be made at Lockheed's Troy, Alabama, and Raytheon's Tucson, Arizona, facilities before shipment for final assembly.

items.headline: Cases against me are medals on my chest: Rahul on U'khand FIR
items.gist: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi said criminal cases filed against him were like "medals on my chest" after Uttarakhand Police registered an FIR accusing him of making alleged casteist remarks against Dalits following his August 29 press conference in support of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. The case followed a complaint by Amit Kumar, who alleged Gandhi's remarks were insulting to Dalits; the Congress said police had not acted against those involved in a 'shudhikaran' purification ceremony at Haldwani's Ramlila Maidan on August 10.

items.headline: Rift in Cong-TVK alliance over 2029 PM candidate
items.gist: Ruptures have appeared in the four-month-old alliance between the Congress and Tamil Nadu's ruling TVK over the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, as TVK ministers push a 'Vijay as PM' narrative while the Congress has threatened to quit the Cabinet if the ruling party refuses to endorse Rahul Gandhi. Tourism Minister S Rajesh Kumar said two Congress ministers would immediately quit if TVK does not accept Rahul Gandhi as the 2029 PM candidate; the TVK government survives on the support of the Congress's five MLAs after failing to secure a majority in the 2026 Assembly election.

items.headline: SC: K'taka already releasing mandated Cauvery river water
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Monday noted that Karnataka was already releasing the mandated quantity of Cauvery river water as it resumed hearing Tamil Nadu's plea for immediate release of its due share, listing the matter again on September 15. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta was told Karnataka released 9,888 cusec against the required 9,000 cusec on August 30 and over 11,000 cusec as of 8 am on Monday; senior advocate Shyam Divan said the state had declared severe drought in parts of the Cauvery basin on August 27.
items.paragraph: The Supreme Court on Monday noted that Karnataka was already releasing the mandated quantity of Cauvery river water as it resumed hearing Tamil Nadu's plea for immediate release of its due share, listing the matter again on September 15. Tamil Nadu claimed a backlog of 17.604 tmcft while Karnataka contested the proportionate calculation method, stating total water ensured at the inter-state border exceeded the required amount by 30,885 cusecs or 2.6 tmcft up to August 31.

items.headline: 'We have no idea where to look': Families await news of 85 missing
items.gist: Five days after flash floods swept Nepal's Rasuwa district on August 26, families of 85 tourists from Tamil Nadu — 36 en route to Kailash Mansarovar and 49 returning to Kathmandu — remain untraceable, while 199 of 305 pilgrims have returned and 21 were rescued. Relatives blocked the Chennai-Tiruchirapalli highway at Singaperumal Kovil on Sunday night demanding updates, saying the Immigration Centre at Gyirong on the Nepal-Tibet border was washed away and urging the Centre to coordinate with China to search the last known location.

items.headline: Rakhi made it to Mumbai. Five days on, sister remains missing
items.gist: Siddharth Kuvavala in Mumbai is still waiting for news of his 48-year-old cousin Shital Chohan, an American citizen of Indian origin from Tennessee, who went missing during the August 26 Nepal-Tibet border floods while on her second Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage with about 50 people organised by Kathmandu-based Himalayan Glacier. A tracker in her bag last placed her at flood-hit Pasang Lhamu on August 26; the Rakhi and sweets she sent from Kathmandu before the disaster now sit on Kuvavala's wrist as her husband and children in the US seek help from the US mission in Kathmandu.

items.headline: Bike mechanic held for rape, murder of nurse in Telangana
items.gist: Hyderabad police on Monday arrested Mohammed Sanaullah, a 34-year-old bike mechanic from Bihar, for allegedly raping and murdering a 21-year-old nurse whose body was found in her room at a private hospital's staff quarters in Tukkuguda, Ranga Reddy district, on August 29. Police said he entered through a window, smothered her when she tried to raise an alarm and raped her while she was unconscious; Shamshabad DCP B Rajesh said he confessed during questioning, and Telangana Nurses Association members protested demanding better safety for healthcare workers.

items.headline: Manipur Deputy CM, 8 MLAs threaten to walk out of govt.
items.gist: Manipur Deputy Chief Minister Losii Dikho and eight other Naga MLAs threatened to pull out of the BJP-led government unless the Centre acts against fellow Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen, whom they accuse of colluding with a Kuki insurgent group, in an August 29 letter hand-delivered to Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday. They demanded arrest of Kuki-Zo leaders over the killing and dismemberment of six Naga civilians whose bodies were recovered on June 10, arrest of Thangboi Kipgen of the Kuki National Front (Presidential) faction, and abrogation of the 2008 Suspension of Operation agreement with 25 Kuki-Zo rebel groups.

Five of the MLAs are from the Naga People’s Front, two from the BJP, one from the NPP, and one Independent.

items.headline: SC refuses pleas against HC order on bail to Goa fire accused
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to entertain pleas challenging a Bombay High Court order setting aside bail granted to nightclub owners Saurav Luthra, Gaurav Luthra and business partner Ajay Gupta in the December 6, 2025 Birch by Romeo Lane fire in Arpora that killed 25 people and injured 50. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu directed the trio to surrender within two weeks and asked the lower court to expedite the trial.

items.headline: Sadhguru pledges Rs 1 cr
items.gist: Spiritual leader Jaggi Vasudev, known as Sadhguru, pledged Rs 1 crore to Nepal's Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund at the 'In Solidarity With Nepal' event in Kathmandu on Sunday following devastating flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border. He proposed urgent creation of a five-nation Himalayan Board involving India, China, Pakistan, Nepal and Bhutan to jointly address natural disasters in the region.

items.headline: RAF denies RTI disclosure on pellet gun use
items.gist: The Rapid Action Force under the CRPF refused former Trinamool MP Saket Gokhale's RTI request for details of pellet-gun firing during the July 20 students' protest, saying the information relates to operational and security matters and does not fall under exceptions for human rights violations. Gokhale, whose first appeal also failed, said he would approach the Supreme Court, arguing CRPF claims use of pellet guns on protesters is not a human rights violation despite allegations of injuries to unarmed youth in the capital.

items.headline: Guj youths beaten for 'reading Malala' threaten protest
items.gist: Members of Students and Youth Collective Ahmedabad and Gujarat Reads Anyway on Monday threatened protest if key suspects are not arrested within 72 hours and demanded a ban on Bajrang Dal from public life after saffron activists allegedly assaulted participants at an August 27 book-reading session in Ahmedabad, objecting to Malala Yousafzai's 'I Am Malala' among other titles. An FIR names Hiren Rabari and Jimit Rabari as alleged key suspects who remain at large; youth groups alleged Bajrang Dal members were present at the police station and that the complaint omitted important details stated by victims.

items.headline: 2 shooters in singer's murder case killed in UP encounter
items.gist: Uttar Pradesh police on Monday shot dead alleged sharpshooters Sumit and Mohit in an encounter on Kairana Road in Shamli district while they were planning to escape to Sonipat in Haryana, five days after singer Anikt Baliyan was sprayed with bullets. items.headline: Top court rejects plea on mandatory ethanol labelling at petrol pumps
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a petition by Narendra Kumar Goswami seeking mandatory display of exact ethanol percentage on every petrol pump dispensing nozzle, fuel receipts and official websites, but granted him liberty to approach the high court concerned. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale found no merit after Attorney General R Venkataramani objected; Goswami argued consumers have a right to know fuel composition and sought a vehicle-compatibility advisory for E20 in the absence of alternatives.

items.headline: SC seeks interrogation records of Abhishek Banerjee's aide
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the West Bengal government to place on record details of the interrogation of Sumit Roy, personal assistant to Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee, and extended his protection from arrest until September 7 in a Salboni land-grabbing case. Roy, challenging a Calcutta High Court denial of pre-arrest bail, alleged investigators questioned him for eight to nine hours daily over 11 days about his family background and Trinamool functioning rather than the alleged land transaction.

items.headline: Goa drops plan to table anti-conversion bill after pushback from minority MLAs
items.gist: The Goa government on Monday decided not to introduce the Goa Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Bill, 2026 during the ongoing monsoon Assembly session after Chief Minister Pramod Sawant met BJP MLAs Michael Lobo and Delilah Lobo and Independent legislator Aleixo Reginaldo Lourenco, who had vowed to oppose it. Lourenco said government data showed no instances of forced religious conversions in Goa; the bill, approved by the state Cabinet days earlier to prohibit conversions through force, coercion, allurement or fraudulent means including marriage, had also drawn opposition from the Congress, AAP and Christian organisations.

items.headline: UP: 11 killed in blast at unlicensed cracker factory
items.gist: Eleven people, including two children, were killed and around 20 injured in a blast at an unlicensed cracker factory in Manauri Bazar, Kaushambi district, about 200 km from Lucknow, on Monday afternoon after a suspected fire triggered a series of explosions heard several kilometres away. Five to six adjacent houses collapsed, rescue teams from Prayagraj and the Army were pressed into service to remove debris, and Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya said a probe would be conducted with stern action against the guilty.

items.headline: 3 Indians rescued by Nepali army in Rasuwa village
items.gist: Three Indian nationals were among four people rescued by the Nepali Army from Chilime village in flood-hit Rasuwa district, Indian Ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava said on Monday. The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu is facilitating their return to India, while India has deployed specialised teams to assist Nepal in rescue operations and victim identification, including a 19-member forensics team in Kathmandu and a tunnel rescue team at hydropower sites in Chilime and Langtang.

items.headline: HDFC Bank shares reverse gains on CEO succession buzz
items.gist: Shares of HDFC Bank Ltd erased early gains after CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan's decision to not seek a reappointment shifted investor focus to uncertainty over succession at India's most-valuable lender. The private lender's shares fell 0.6% after earlier rising as much as 2.7%, with Macquarie Group analyst Suresh Ganapathy saying leadership uncertainty may keep the stock in a narrow range as attention turns to finding a successor five months after part-time Chairman Atanu Chakraborty abruptly resigned.

items.headline: ONGC to invest Rs 1L cr in deepwater push
items.gist: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation said on Monday it will invest Rs 1 lakh crore in deepwater exploration in the next five years, drilling seven deepwater oil and gas wells this year and targeting 10 next year, with plans to drill 87 deepwater wells over the period. Chairman and CEO Arun Kumar Singh said ONGC also plans to set up its international crude and products trading platform by the end of this fiscal year, with Dubai and Singapore likely to serve as the base.

items.headline: 14 years on... still failing our daughters
items.gist: A 16-year-old from Mainpuri in Uttar Pradesh who boarded a bus in Greater Noida on the rainy night of August 4 was allegedly gang-raped by the conductor and driver and abandoned at Kashmere Gate, more than 40 km away, police said. The Class 11 student had mistakenly got off at Pari Chowk around 9 pm while heading to her cousin's home in Noida Sector 63; bus driver Kuldeep (39) and conductor Sandeep (26) have been arrested from a parking lot.

items.headline: Sonia Gandhi memoir: Penguin cites 'particular issue'
items.gist: Penguin Random House India said on Monday there was no external pressure behind its decision not to publish Sonia Gandhi's memoir, citing an impasse over "a particular issue" during discussions on "Belonging: A Journey of Love" without disclosing the contentious matter. The clarification comes amid controversy after US-based Alfred A Knopf announced a November 10 release, while Congress leaders including Ashok Gehlot have alleged governmental pressure, with Gehlot claiming sections relating to Prime Minister Narendra Modi were targeted for removal.

items.headline: India fastest growing economy with 7.8 pc in Q1
items.gist: India's economy grew at a faster-than-expected 7.8 per cent in the April–June quarter, slowing from 8.6 per cent in the previous quarter but remaining well above expectations and exceeding the Reserve Bank of India's forecast of 7 per cent. The growth showed resilience despite concerns that the war in Iran and global economic uncertainty could weigh on expansion and disrupt energy markets.

items.headline: 3-yr-old nursery student abused; school bus driver held
items.gist: A school bus driver has been arrested for allegedly sexually abusing a three-year-old nursery student of a private school in Delhi's Bawana area, police said. The incident came to light on August 19 after the child's family noticed injuries; on August 24 she identified the accused from photographs and CCTV footage, and an FIR was registered under the POCSO Act.

items.headline: AIMIM worker stabbed to death by gang in Hyderabad
items.gist: An AIMIM worker, Mahboob Ali (in his mid-50s), was stabbed to death by a gang of five people near his residence at Vattepally in Hyderabad on Sunday night and died in hospital; police said the assailants were engaged by a relative of the deceased. AIMIM MLA Mohammed Mubeen visited the bereaved family and Falaknuma Police Station, urging strict action; a murder case was registered based on a complaint by the deceased's son and further investigation is underway.

items.headline: Adopt 'guerrilla strategy', Jarange urges Marathas
items.gist: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange on Monday urged community members to adopt a "guerrilla strategy," quietly move towards Mumbai and prepare for a major agitation if the government fails to implement demands by September 12, as his indefinite hunger strike at Antarwali Sarati in Jalna entered its third day. Jarange refused IV fluids on Sunday despite low blood sugar, claimed 58 lakh Kunbi genealogical records were found for Marathas, and said even if he died his body should be taken to Mumbai for the agitation.

items.headline: AP CM inaugurates Veligonda irrigation project Phase-1
items.gist: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Monday inaugurated Phase-1 of the Veligonda irrigation project, releasing Krishna water into Nallamala Sagar to provide irrigation to 1.19 lakh acres and drinking water to four lakh people with 10.70 TMC entering the reservoir. The NDA government has spent more than Rs 2,400 crore on Veligonda in two years, disbursed Rs 768 crore to displaced families within 48 days, and the fully operational project is expected to irrigate 4.47 lakh acres across 30 mandals and benefit around 23 lakh people.

items.headline: The cost of parliamentary silence
items.gist: Parliament has again been adjourned sine die without prorogation 17 days after the Monsoon Session ended, amid speculation the government could call a special sitting to revive the delimitation Bill defeated in April's Budget Session; repeated disruptions consumed time meant for debate, legislation and scrutiny. Joseph T R of Bengaluru writes that while a frequently cited PRS estimate puts the cost of running Parliament at ₹2.5 lakh per minute, that 2012 figure is outdated and the financial loss is only part of the story.

items.headline: Bangladesh crime video falsely linked to WB, BJP workers
items.gist: A disturbing video showing recovery of a rape and murder victim's body in Bangladesh is being falsely shared on social media as an incident from West Bengal involving BJP workers, Boom established through reverse image search. The video was recorded in Shibchar, Madaripur district, Bangladesh, showing recovery of 28-year-old Shampa Khatun's body on August 19; Faruk Mollah was arrested on August 21, and the false claim comes amid clashes between ABVP and Left-backed student groups at Jadavpur University on August 20.

items.headline: This professor runs a public library from her home
items.gist: Prof Madhu Khanna, an Oxford doctorate holder in Indology and former director at Jamia Millia Islamia, maintains the Tantra Foundation Library at Hari Bhari Farm in Chhattarpur, Delhi, actively inviting researchers in art, archaeology, Indology and religion unlike many private academic collections that remain locked. The 1970s modernist residence housing the library reflects early Chhattarpur farmhouse architecture and offers scholars access to her seminal work on Tantra and goddess-centred Shakta traditions.

items.headline: Dispute over buffalo passage turns violent; one killed
items.gist: A dispute between two groups over taking a buffalo through a plot turned violent in Milawali village, Etah district, Uttar Pradesh, on Sunday evening, leaving eight people injured and Shyampal, 36, dead while being taken to a higher medical centre around 3 am on Monday. Police said Mukesh was returning from fields with his buffalo through Shyampal's plot when an objection led to a clash involving sticks, batons and an axe; four people from each side were injured.

items.headline: Attempt to suppress voices, says Cong on FIR
items.gist: The Congress lashed out at the BJP after an FIR was filed in Uttarakhand against Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on a 'shuddhikaran ceremony' at the venue where party chief Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a rally, calling it an attempt to divert attention and suppress voices. Jairam Ramesh and K C Venugopal said Gandhi had demanded action against BJP workers involved in purification after Kharge's rally, but an FIR was filed against Gandhi the next day instead of against the accused.

items.headline: 'Smash the patriarchy': Minister responds to remarks on confining women to homes
items.gist: Kerala Higher Education Minister Roji M John hit out at remarks seeking to confine women to their homes, ending a Facebook post with "SMASH THE PATRIARCHY," two days after Rahul Gandhi lashed out at the Manusmriti mindset. Though he did not name anyone, the post came a day after Islamic scholar Kanthapuram A P Aboobacker Musliyar said at a Kochi conference that bringing women onto public platforms causes "great destruction" and that Islam mandated purdah; Roji recalled Kerala's history of women's struggles including the Guruvayur Satyagraha and leaders such as Dakshayani Velayudhan and Accamma Cherian.

items.headline: Govt considering easing FDI norms in defence
items.gist: The government is considering liberalisation of foreign direct investment norms in the defence sector, with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade holding stakeholder consultations; some easing is under consideration, an official said on Monday. Currently FDI up to 74 per cent is permitted through the automatic route and beyond that through government approval where modern technology access is likely, subject to MHA security clearance; India attracted USD 32.29 million FDI in defence industries between April 2000 and March 2026.

items.headline: Maruti Suzuki raises capex to Rs 77,500 cr
items.gist: Maruti Suzuki India has increased its capex outlay to Rs 77,500 crore for five years till FY31 for capacity expansion, new models and R&D, Managing Director and CEO Hisashi Takeuchi said at the AGM on Monday. Capex for FY26-27 alone is planned at Rs 14,000 crore, a 40 per cent jump from around Rs 10,000 crore last year, and he assured Maruti cars from production year 2008 are compatible with E20 fuel.

items.headline: Zomato bans analogue dishes on its platform
items.gist: Food delivery aggregator Zomato on Monday announced a zero-tolerance policy on sale of analogue dishes including analogue cheese, paneer or other dairy products, reserving the right to delist non-compliant restaurants with immediate effect. Dishes declared as containing analogue dairy have been delisted, following renewed food safety focus after Maharashtra FDA crackdowns and FSSAI inspections in Delhi five-star hotels.

items.headline: Centre's FY27 fiscal deficit touches 26.8 pc of full year target at end July
items.gist: The central government's fiscal deficit for 2026-27 stood at 26.8 per cent of the full-year target at the end of July, at Rs 4,55,144 crore in the April-July period against a target of 4.3 per cent of GDP or Rs 16.96 lakh crore, according to CGA data released on Monday. Net tax revenue was about Rs 8.45 lakh crore or 29.5 per cent of budget estimates and total expenditure was about Rs 17.62 lakh crore or 32.9 per cent of BE.

items.headline: Ex-mill sugar prices fall 30%; retail rates same
items.gist: Ex-mill sugar prices fell nearly 30 per cent to Rs 47 per kg on Monday from a peak of Rs 67 per kg on August 18 following government interventions, but the drop has yet to filter to retail shelves as retailers hold stock bought at higher rates. Retail sugar was selling at Rs 64.23 per kg on Sunday against a wholesale rate of Rs 59.72 per kg, and an estimated 3-3.5 lakh tonnes of export-refined sugar is expected to enter the domestic market over the next two months.

items.headline: Govt: IOC boosted LPG output by 30%
items.gist: State-owned Indian Oil Corporation ramped up liquefied petroleum gas production by nearly 30 per cent and kept refineries operating above 100 per cent utilisation as Strait of Hormuz disruptions threatened India's energy supplies, chairman Arvinder Singh Sahney said at the 67th AGM on Monday. IOC diversified crude sourcing and secured alternative supplies as West Asia conflict disrupted global energy markets; India imports more than 88 per cent of its crude oil requirement.

items.headline: Investments by PE/VC funds jump to $4.1 bln
items.gist: Private equity and venture capital funds' investments in India increased 3 per cent year-on-year to USD 4.1 billion in July, 52 per cent higher than USD 2.7 billion in June, according to an EY-IVCA report released on Monday. July recorded 10 large deals totalling USD 2.8 billion including Brookfield's USD 600 million bet in Lumara, with buyout investments accounting for USD 1.4 billion, a 176 per cent jump from July 2025.

items.headline: Mahindra to manufacture parts for Airbus A320 plane
items.gist: Mahindra Aerostructures on Monday said it secured a contract from Airbus to manufacture and supply fuselage skins for A320 aircraft with delivery targeted for 2028, covering Sections 18 and 19 of the A320neo and A321XLR rear fuselage and tail sections. Components will be manufactured at Mahindra's Bengaluru facility and supplied to Airbus' Augsburg facility in Germany, expanding India's role in the global aerospace supply chain.

items.headline: Chandra's dissenting lenders Canara Bank, Union Bank move NCLAT
items.gist: Dissenting lenders of Subhash Chandra on Monday moved NCLAT challenging the NCLT order approving a Rs 6.5 crore payment by the Essel Group chairman over creditor claims of about Rs 22,006.57 crore in his personal insolvency resolution process. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for LIC Housing Finance, Canara Bank and Union Bank, sought urgent hearing saying the order would defeat the purpose of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code; NCLAT listed the matter for Tuesday.

items.headline: Bank of Baroda to recruit 2,482 Local Bank Officers
items.gist: Bank of Baroda will recruit 2,482 Local Bank Officers in Junior Management Grade Scale-I (JMGS-1) on a regular basis across 20 States and Union Territories, including Karnataka, with selected officers posted in the State they apply for during the first 12 years of service or until promotion to SMGS-IV, whichever is earlier. Online applications are open until September 7, 2026; candidates must be 21–30 as of September 1, 2026, graduates from a recognised university, fluent in the local language of the State they apply from, and a minimum of one year’s post-qualification experience as an officer in a Scheduled Commercial Bank is also desired.

items.headline: Keralam CM orders SIT to probe Messi event row
items.gist: Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan directed the Home Department to constitute an SIT for an anti-corruption and suspected tax fraud inquiry into the previous LDF government’s endeavour to bring the 2021 FIFA World Cup-winning Argentina team and Lionel Messi for a friendly exhibition match at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Kochi in August 2025.
items.paragraph: Keralam Chief Minister V.D. A finance department inquiry found the sponsor, a news broadcasting company, wire-transferred ₹126 crore to a foreign entity in 2025, triggering a service tax obligation of ₹22.68 crore; he also ordered a probe of a suspected conspiracy to defraud the treasury.

items.headline: V-dem’s democracy index rates India at its lowest since 1975
items.gist: Sambavi Parthasarathy and Gauri Singavarapu report that the UN CERD’s concern over large-scale voter exclusion, including of Muslims, in the Special Intensive Revision aligns with the V-Dem Institute’s latest electoral democracy index, released in March, which rates India at its lowest since 1975 Emergency rule. V-Dem listed India among countries “autocratising” slowly; scores on judicial accountability and corruption, Election Management Body autonomy, and impartial administration are at their lowest in 50 years.

items.headline: Efforts to improve life of Sikkim Lepchas
items.gist: A fifty-years-ago reprint dated Gangtok, August 31, 1976, reported that a detailed land survey had started in Dzongu, North Sikkim, as a step toward land reforms for Lepchas, then about 15% of the State’s population. Elders at a meeting at Tingbhum in Dzongu passed a resolution favouring changes in their way of life, especially expenses on marriage.

items.headline: Congress calls GDP numbers ‘Greatly Distorted Picture’
items.gist: Congress communication chief Jairam Ramesh questioned the 7.8% GDP growth recorded in the April–June quarter, calling it a “Greatly Distorted Picture” of the economy. He said private investment sentiment was depressed, consumer confidence had fallen to its lowest level since the COVID-19 pandemic, and flagged the trade deficit with China, falling household savings and record household debt.

items.headline: After hottest August, bleak outlook for September rain
items.gist: The IMD on Monday forecast September rainfall at least 9% short of the long-period average of 167.9 mm after India recorded the hottest August since 1901, with mean temperature 28.01 degrees Celsius, about 0.67 degree above normal, and the highest average minimum of 24.36 degrees Celsius. As of August 31, cumulative monsoon rainfall was about 14% below normal; August rain was 213.3 mm, the seventh-lowest since 2001.

items.headline: Five-member NCLT Bench to hear Subhash Chandra case
items.gist: The NCLT on Monday formed a five-member Bench, the first in its history, to decide media baron Subhash Chandra’s repayment plan in a personal insolvency case involving claims of more than ₹22,000 crore after a Division Bench failed to reach a majority on a proposed ₹6.5 crore repayment plan. items.headline: India’s GDP growth at 7.8% in Q1, slower than last quarter but quicker than last year
items.gist: India’s GDP grew 7.8% in April–June 2026 (Q1 FY27), quicker than 6.9% in Q1 last year but slower than 8.6% in January–March 2026; Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said nominal GDP grew 10.3% and real GVA 8.2%. items.headline: What goes on behind the screen when you pay through UPI?
items.gist: Vasudevan Mukunth explains that UPI, operated by NPCI, processed 2,366 crore transactions in July 2026 worth nearly ₹30 lakh crore (around 7,600 per second); in 2025-26 it handled 24,160 crore transactions worth ₹314 lakh crore, 85% of India’s digital payments by volume and 49% of real-time payments worldwide in 2025 according to the IMF. Raghuram Rajan piloted UPI in April 2016 with 21 banks; it crossed 100 crore transactions a month in October 2019.

items.headline: Move from 'endless war': PM tells Putin
items.gist: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to move away from the "endless war" with Ukraine towards an "end to the war", and assured Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian of India's support to resolve Iran's conflict with the United States and Israel, during separate meetings on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek. Modi said every day spent in war sets humanity back and that a peaceful resolution was essential; Putin replied, "We are moving in this direction," as the meetings came less than a fortnight before Modi would host both leaders at the BRICS summit in New Delhi.

items.headline: Nepal flood toll 900; over 4,200 still missing
items.gist: The toll in devastating flash floods and mudslides caused by a glacial collapse in Nepal has gone over 900, with more than 4,200 people reported missing, including 590 foreign nationals and 99 security personnel. Triggered by a wave of ice, rocks, and debris along the Bhote Koshi River, the disaster has affected central and northern regions, leaving at least 933 workers trapped across six hydropower projects; Prime Minister Balendra Shah called it an "unimaginable and heartbreaking" calamity.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pak agree to defence pact secretariat
items.gist: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan agreed to establish a secretariat in Saudi Arabia under their Mecca joint defence agreement, which will initially be headed by a Pakistani secretary-general for three years, Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry said on Monday. Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stressed after the first ministerial meeting in Istanbul that the regional defence pact was not aimed at any particular country and was open to others, including Egypt, committing the three nations to mutual defence if any of them is attacked.

items.headline: 100-yr-old temple demolished
items.gist: A more than century-old Hindu temple has been demolished, reportedly to incorporate its land into a madrassa in Pakistan's Punjab province, with local residents, minority groups and a political party saying religious zealots demolished the shrine on August 21. Occupying approximately 1,000 square metres in Siraj village in Narowal, about 130 km from Lahore, the 100- to 125-year-old temple was torn down by members of the banned far-right Tehreek-i-Labbaik Pakistan, while the government claimed the structure collapsed due to torrential rains.

items.gist: A workers' strike has disrupted air traffic at Kenya's main airport in Nairobi, leaving many travellers stranded after flights were delayed or cancelled, the Kenya Airports Authority said on Monday. items.headline: Indian charged for murder
items.gist: A 25-year-old Indian national, Muruganathan Kathirvel, was on Monday charged with murder in Singapore for allegedly killing Indian-origin Raj Maheshkumar on August 29 by slashing his neck with a chopper. Police said they received a call for assistance at about 10.10 pm on August 29 in an industrial zone on Singapore's west coast, where the 29-year-old victim was found lying motionless on the road and pronounced dead at the scene.

items.headline: UN committee says countries must consider reparations for slave trade
items.gist: A UN committee said countries are legally obliged to consider reparations for the transatlantic slave trade and take other measures to address the enduring legacy of racial discrimination, in guidance published Monday by the Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination. The document, describing a "paradigm shift" away from debates over historical responsibility, states that obligations arise from the 1965 convention on racial discrimination and urges "transformative" measures including opening archives, revising public memorials and establishing independent truth commissions, noting at least 12.5 million Africans were taken and sold between the 15th and 19th centuries.

items.gist: North Korea said on Monday the United States' hostile policy remained unchanged and vowed to continue strengthening its nuclear force, rejecting repeated U.S. calls for its denuclearisation.
items.paragraph: North Korea said on Monday the United States' hostile policy remained unchanged and vowed to continue strengthening its nuclear force, rejecting repeated U.S. calls for its denuclearisation. items.headline: Trump vows 'hard' response after fresh exchange of fire with Iran
items.gist: Donald Trump threatened to hit Iran "hard" after the two foes traded fire for the first time in over a month, with the US saying it carried out strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on the island of Larak in the Strait of Hormuz and Iran retaliating with missile and drone attacks aimed at Jordan and the United Arab Emirates. State media reported two people were killed in the US attack on Larak, while President Masoud Pezeshkian later called for dialogue, saying continuing the war was neither in Iran's interest nor in the interest of the region.

items.headline: Indonesia's Sinabung volcano erupts
items.gist: Mount Sinabung in Indonesia erupted on Monday, spewing a column of black ash and smoke 3,500 metres from the summit over Sumatra island, with no immediate reports of casualties or evacuations but residents advised to refrain from activities within 6 kilometres of the summit. Officials raised the volcano alert level to "Watch," the second-highest level, as several villages in Karo district were covered in grey ash and masks were distributed.

Chief Minister Sohail Afridi condemned the attack as cowardly and a search operation was launched to trace the perpetrators.

items.headline: Nepal tunnel workers recount horror and ordeal
items.gist: Workers from Nepal's flood-hit hydropower projects described desperate escapes, including Shiva Giri and colleagues who trekked 12 hours through forest after the Mailung Hydropower Project was swamped, as rescue teams try to trace 933 workers out of contact since August 26 with more than 600 believed stranded inside tunnels. So far 279 people have been rescued from tunnels and expert teams from India and China have joined Nepal's efforts.

items.headline: Lawyer, activist & aid giver win this year's Magsaysay awards
items.gist: Singaporean lawyer Tommy Koh, Myanmar activist Bo Kyi and Bangladeshi aid worker Runa Khan were named winners of the 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Awards on Monday. Koh was recognised for presiding over the 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea conference, Bo Kyi for documenting human rights atrocities after seven years in prison, and Runa Khan for aid work that now employs more than 7,500 people through hospital ships and land-based hospitals.

items.headline: 15 missing in flash floods in Grand Canyon
items.gist: A major flash flood at the Grand Canyon left one person dead and about 15 others missing or unaccounted for, with scores of visitors evacuated and the only water pipeline for tourists and residents destroyed. Emergency water restrictions began Monday preventing overnight stays at lodges, and the body of a 46-year-old man was recovered Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River.

items.headline: Nashville says final farewell to Dolly Parton
items.gist: US country music legend Dolly Parton was laid to rest in a private family ceremony at Nashville's Woodlawn Memorial Park beside her late husband Carl Dean after her death at 80 following a brief battle with cancer. items.paragraph: In the first top-level Iran–India meeting since the war on Iran began in February, Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on the sidelines of the SCO summit and urged him to ensure peace and stability in West Asia and freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz; the MEA said he called for freedom of navigation and commerce and that civilians and civilian infrastructure, including commercial shipping and seafarers, must not be harmed. Mr. Pezeshkian blamed Israel and the U.S. for the conflict and asked Mr. Modi to use India’s extensive contacts with various parties to help the dialogue process. After the meeting Mr. Modi said on X he reiterated commitment to strengthening India’s long-standing friendship with Iran, expanding and diversifying the trade basket, and that India will continue to support efforts for lasting peace, and that he looked forward to welcoming Mr. Pezeshkian to India for the upcoming BRICS summit.

items.headline: Marconi’s new invention
items.gist: A hundred-years-ago reprint from an August 29, 1926 London cable said Signor Marconi had experimented with a special loud speaker giving great amplification, believing the voice could carry twenty miles. He was leaving for Italy in the yacht Electra on September 1 to test beam strength between England and Canada and England and South Africa.

items.headline: Five Palestinians killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza City, medics say

items.headline: UN panel presents legal case for broad slavery reparations
items.gist: The UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination said on Monday that states parties must implement comprehensive reparatory measures for people of African descent covering monetary, non-monetary and structural remedies for harms from the transatlantic African slave trade. At least 12.5 million Africans were taken and sold between the 15th and 19th centuries; committee member Pela Boker-Wilson said the findings carry authoritative weight though they are not legally binding.

items.gist: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on Monday there were signs Russia and Israel had spread disinformation over Spain’s migration policy that triggered last month’s rush of migrants into Ceuta, but no evidence of Moroccan involvement. Over 72,000 migrants irregularly crossed from Morocco into Ceuta between July 30 and 31, with at least 100 people dying in the attempt according to local authorities; about 5,000 have stayed in Ceuta.

items.headline: Final whistle: Messi calls time on glittering career
items.gist: After mesmerising the football world for over two decades and winning nearly every accolade, Lionel Messi announced he was done playing for Argentina, following the team's 1-0 loss to Spain in the July FIFA World Cup Final where the 39-year-old scored eight goals. The decision became clearer after his father Jorge Messi died on August 7; Messi had briefly retired after Argentina's 2016 Copa America final loss to Chile but reversed that decision and went on to win two Copa Americas and the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar.

items.headline: Asian Games-bound horse infected, sparks testing row
items.gist: India will be down one rider-horse combination in three-day eventing at the 2026 Asian Games after Captain Aahan Kumar's horse Bolivar Gio Granno tested positive for Piroplasmosis, with reserve rider Pradeep Jhangam alleging the Equestrian Federation of India's ad-hoc committee failed to send his horse's blood sample required by August 17. Lt Col Sandeep Dewan of the ad-hoc panel disputed the allegations, saying selected riders based abroad had given undertakings that their horses were fit and that mandatory pre-quarantine testing was conducted by the official Asian Games transporter, with Bolivar Gio Granno's positive result communicated on the evening of August 25.
