items.headline: Karnataka youngsters dominate Day 1
items.gist: Karnataka's young tennis players were at the centre of an action-packed opening round at the KSLTA World Tennis Tour Junior J30 Bengaluru at the SM Krishna Tennis Stadium on Monday, with closely fought contests across boys' and girls' singles. Notable results included third seed Niyanth Badri Narayanan (USA) beating Manan Rai 6-4, 6-1, top seed Shaivi Gaurav Dalal defeating Dhaanvi D Kanjithanda 6-2, 6-1, and third seed Disha Kumar edging Sidhhi Pandey 6-1, 6-7 (3), 7-5.

items.headline: Ailing Djokovic makes shock exit
items.gist: Novak Djokovic suffered his earliest Grand Slam exit in 20 years on Sunday, beaten by Argentina's Mariano Navone 7-6 (7/5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 in the US Open first round, ending his run of 78 Grand Slam first-round victories dating back to 2006. The 39-year-old vomited on court and struggled with late-match cramps and back pain, saying he has carried such physical problems "pretty much every match this year," while 46-year-old Venus Williams also lost in straight sets to compatriot Sofia Kenin 6-2, 7-6 (6).

items.gist: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blasted 92 off 81 balls to become the youngest batter to score a Duleep Trophy half-century, breaking a 57-year-old record held by the late Laxman Singh, as East Zone were bowled out for 266—identical to Central Zone's first-innings total—in the semifinal in Bengaluru on Monday. Left-arm spinner Harsh Dubey took 4 for 66 as East lost 10 wickets for 105 runs after Sooryavanshi and Abhimanyu Easwaran's 161-run opening stand, leaving Central at 45 for three at stumps in their second essay.

items.headline: Persistence pays off for South
items.gist: Captain Tilak Varma made an unbeaten 106 off 225 balls and Shreyas Gopal scored 87 as South Zone finished at 285 for nine on day two of the Duleep Trophy semifinal against North Zone in Bengaluru, taking a first-innings lead of 90 runs after North were bowled out for 195. Gurnoor Brar took 4 for 70 as South recovered from 80 for five through a 175-run sixth-wicket stand between Tilak and Gopal, though South lost three wickets for two runs in the last 30 minutes of play.

items.headline: New playing conditions for K Thimmappiah Memorial
items.gist: The Karnataka State Cricket Association has made three significant rule changes to its flagship four-day Dr (Capt) K Thimmappiah memorial tournament kicking off across Bengaluru and Mysuru on Tuesday to encourage teams to pursue victory rather than play for a draw. Each team is limited to 120 overs in the first innings and 60 in the second—with half of any unused first-innings overs added to the second—teams can take the new ball after 70 overs and must take it after 90, and fielding sides may have no more than three fielders outside the inner circle after completing one-third of their maximum overs in the second innings.

items.headline: Shafali calls for assessment after batting implosion
items.gist: India opener Shafali Verma said the team's batting unit will assess its shortcomings on turners despite opening the Women's Asia Cup with a 94-run victory over Thailand in Dubai, where India slumped from 91 for one to 159 for nine after her 64 off 36 balls. Shafali said the track offered hold and turn with the older ball and credited Thailand's bowlers, acknowledging she could have played the ball better after it gripped and arrived a little late.

items.headline: Pak set to send Rizwan, Imam back home
items.gist: Pakistan are likely to send wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan and opening batter Imam-Ul-Haq back home from their tour of England, where the team has endured heavy defeats in the first two Tests by an innings and 103 runs at Leeds and by 194 runs at Lord's. Geo News reported the decision following a high-level meeting of Pakistan Cricket Board officials including chairman Mohsin Naqvi, COO Sumair Ahmed and head coach for limited-overs cricket Mike Hesson.

items.headline: 5-star room shortage hits Asiad cricket: official
items.gist: The Asian Cricket Council has heard concerns over a lack of five-star hotel accommodation for players at the upcoming Asian Games in Japan, Sri Lanka Cricket secretary Prakash Schaffter said on Monday. Men's and women's T20 cricket will be played at Japan's newly-built cricket ground in Nisshin starting September 17, and member states have agreed to send representatives to examine grounds and logistical arrangements while hoping the tournament will still go ahead.

items.headline: Nivaan, Krupa wear U-15 chess title
items.gist: Nivaan Raghavendra and Krupa S Ukkali won the open and girls titles at the Janamitra Karnataka Chess U-15 Championships in Hassan District, each scoring seven points. Nivaan took first place ahead of Yeshas H, Indrajit Majumdar and Venkata Naga K M in a four-way tie, while Krupa edged Simran Nadaf and Indusheetala by 0.5 points, with the top four from both categories qualifying for the U-15 National Championships.

items.headline: Lionel Messi bids emotional farewell to Argentina after international retirement
items.gist: Football icon Lionel Messi announced through his official Instagram profile that he has retired from international football and will no longer wear the Argentina jersey, saying he made the decision two days after the World Cup final loss to Spain. Messi said it was a decision that still hurts deeply but that he always gave everything for the shirt and leaves with pride in moments shared with teammates.

items.headline: Mourinho calls for patience with Diomande
items.gist: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho called for patience with Ivory Coast winger Yan Diomande, a reported $146 million signing from Leipzig who has made three substitute appearances without replicating his Bundesliga or World Cup form. Mourinho said Diomande needs to go "little by little" after Madrid's 4-0 win over Malaga, their third from three league games this season.

items.headline: Venus Williams bows out of her 26th US Open
items.gist: Venus Williams bowed out of her 26th US Open singles appearance early Monday, losing 6-2, 7-6 (6) to fellow American wild card Sofia Kenin after not getting on court until midnight in what could be her final singles match at a Grand Slam. The 46-year-old has lost 15 consecutive singles matches dating to July 2025 and said her mind was fully focused on recovering for doubles with sister Serena later in the week.

items.headline: Djokovic crashes out in US Open first round for first time
items.gist: Novak Djokovic was knocked out in the US Open first round for the first time, beaten by Mariano Navone of Argentina 7-6 (5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 after more than 4 1/2 hours in which the 39-year-old vomited and battled leg problems. The 24-time Grand Slam champion had been 19-0 in US Open first rounds and had not lost an opening major match since the 2006 Australian Open.

items.headline: England's Robinson-Archer combo seals series
items.gist: Ollie Robinson and Jofra Archer took 24 of Pakistan's 38 possible wickets in harness together for the first time in Test cricket as England clinched the series 2-0 against Pakistan at Lord's on Sunday with a day and a game to spare. Change bowlers Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson claimed the other 14 wickets; the third and last Test starts on September 9 at Edgbaston.

items.headline: Messi bids goodbye after 21 magical years
items.gist: Lionel Messi, 39, ended his Argentina career after 125 goals in 207 matches, the national records for appearances and goals, writing that the decision still hurts but the time had come; he drafted the letter on July 21, two days after losing the World Cup final to Spain, and delayed publishing it because his father Jorge Messi died in Rosario on August 8. He won the World Cup in Qatar in 2022 and Copa América in 2021 and 2024 after briefly retiring in 2016.

items.headline: Exceptional Sooryavanshi the focal point at the CoE
items.gist: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made 92 off 81 balls (seven sixes, seven fours) in 118 minutes for East Zone against Central Zone, adding 161 for the opening wicket with Abhimanyu Easwaran (69). He became the youngest half-centurion in Duleep Trophy history, breaking Laxman Singh’s record from January 1969 when Singh was 16, before being caught at deep mid-wicket off Harsh Dubey.

items.headline: UNDP internships: Gateways to a global career
items.gist: For Indian students interested in international development, public policy, economics, sustainability, communications or global affairs, a UNDP internship can offer practical exposure across offices including the Washington Representation Office, which currently offers General and Communications & Outreach internships. UNDP internships are generally open to final-year bachelor's students, master's students and recent graduates who begin within one year of graduation, with applications requiring tailored cover letters and CVs connecting skills to each role; students can also explore opportunities with UNDP India covering sustainable development, climate resilience and the Sustainable Development Goals.

items.headline: Nutrition guide for healthy hair and regrowth
items.gist: Hair is primarily composed of keratin and requires adequate protein, iron, omega-3 fatty acids, B-vitamins, zinc, selenium and vitamins C and E for follicular health; deficiency can cause premature resting phase and increased shedding. The article recommends eggs, berries, spinach, fatty fish, nuts and sweet potatoes while advising against refined sugars, crash dieting and excessive alcohol or caffeine, noting consistent nutritional changes generally take 3 to 6 months to show results.

items.headline: Understanding conjunctivitis or eye flu
items.gist: Conjunctivitis, commonly called eye flu or pink eye, is inflammation of the conjunctiva causing dilated blood vessels and a pink appearance, with types including viral, bacterial, allergic and chemical or irritant forms. Viral and bacterial forms are highly contagious while allergic conjunctivitis is not; management ranges from supportive care and antibiotics where appropriate to avoiding triggers and immediate flushing for chemical exposure, with medical evaluation advised for severe pain, light sensitivity, blurred vision or symptoms persisting beyond five days.

items.headline: Controlling anger before it controls you
items.gist: Unmanaged temper stems from an overactive fight-or-flight response and can erode relationships, health and peace of mind; learning to control anger means shifting from impulsive reaction to intentional response. Immediate strategies include a 5-to-10-second pause, controlled box breathing, and physical disengagement from heated conversations, while long-term techniques involve trigger mapping, cognitive reframing and assertive "I" statements, with professional support such as CBT recommended for persistent outbursts.

items.headline: NIT-K associate prof. Shashi Bhushan receives ECSI award
items.gist: Shashi Bhushan Arya, associate professor in the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering at NIT-K Surathkal, received the Electrochemical Society of India’s S.K. Seshadri Memorial Mascot National Award–2026, with a cash prize of ₹25,000, for work on industrial corrosion science, prevention, monitoring, pipeline integrity, and sustainable surface engineering.
items.paragraph: Shashi Bhushan Arya, associate professor in the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering at NIT-K Surathkal, received the Electrochemical Society of India’s S.K. Seshadri Memorial Mascot National Award–2026, with a cash prize of ₹25,000, for work on industrial corrosion science, prevention, monitoring, pipeline integrity, and sustainable surface engineering. The award was presented during the 33rd NSEST–2026 at JRD Tata Auditorium, IISc, Bengaluru, on Friday and Saturday by Shubha V. Iyengar, Padma Shri awardee and former distinguished scientist at CSIR-NAL. He delivered a lecture titled “Flow-Driven Internal Corrosion of Petroleum Pipelines: Mechanisms, Monitoring, and Mitigation.”

items.headline: Govt notifies Rs 1,27,500-crore Semicon 2.0 programme
items.gist: The government on Monday notified a Rs 1.27 lakh crore Semicon 2.0 programme, offering fiscal support across the semiconductor value chain including 40% funding for large silicon wafer fabs with a minimum investment threshold of Rs 20,000 crore. The programme, approved by the Union Cabinet in July with an outlay of Rs 1,27,500 crore, covers six pillars and 10 categories spanning chip design, semiconductor equipment and materials, fabrication, packaging, R&D and talent creation, with IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw saying the application window is open now.

items.headline: Amaravati to get India's first dedicated univ for quantum tech, AI and other deep-tech
items.gist: Andhra Pradesh has approved India's first dedicated Quantum and Artificial Intelligence University campus in Amaravati, spearheaded by NIELIT and fully funded by MeitY at Rs 730 crore on 8.5 acres in the CRDA region. The campus will offer programmes in quantum computing, AI, semiconductors and other deep-tech areas, train approximately 8,250 learners over five years, and until completion academic programmes will run at Acharya Nagarjuna University in Guntur.

items.headline: Enhancing safety in wilderness
items.gist: Rajeshwari Gopal of Mangaluru writes that the Karnataka Forest Department's decision to make GPS tracking devices compulsory for all trekkers across the state's forest routes is a step in the right direction, as eco-tourism grows on Western Ghats trails such as Kudremukh and Kodachadri where lost hikers and delayed search operations have become recurring concerns. She argues that satellite-enabled tracking ensures real-time monitoring and swift emergency response, though technology alone cannot replace ecological discipline.

items.headline: 6 scientists, 120 research papers, 1 big bet—this IISc startup aims to put India on GaN map
items.gist: Bengaluru startup Agnit Semiconductors, born at IISc's Innovation Centre, has become India's first Gallium Nitride-based semiconductor company with a team of seven researchers and over 15 years of collective GaN experience aiming to design and manufacture GaN-powered semiconductors within five years. CEO Hareesh Chandrasekar said India is not too far behind in GaN technology and can catch up with government incentives under National Semiconductor Mission 2.0's Rs 1,27,500 crore outlay.

items.headline: TN govt increases milk procurement prices
items.gist: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay announced in the Assembly on Monday a further hike in Aavin milk procurement prices from Rs 41 to Rs 44 per litre, entailing an additional Rs 60 crore monthly or Rs 720 crore annual outlay, following an earlier hike from Rs 38 to Rs 41 on August 19. Vijay also unveiled major infrastructure investments including Rs 33,066 crore for the Tamil Nadu Transmission Improvement Scheme, a Rs 20,800 crore 1,600 MW super critical thermal plant in Tuticorin, a Rs 175 crore semiconductor park at Maduramangalam, a Rs 400 crore FinTech Hub in Coimbatore and a multi-modal logistics hub in Tiruchirapalli.

items.headline: Can AI help save the planet and help build peace?
items.gist: Deepika Amirapu writes that artificial intelligence can serve as an early-warning system for farmers, traffic, forest fires and floods, connecting Sustainable Development Goals to everyday struggles over water, food and energy in cities such as Bengaluru. She argues AI can analyse climate, food, migration and economic conditions to flag rising risks before crises erupt, though Green AI is essential because data centres consume enormous electricity and water, and educational institutions should encourage students to solve real societal problems with AI.

items.headline: Japan plans defence boost with drones, AI and missiles
items.gist: Japan plans to use drones, AI and new methods of warfare as it adapts its defence strategies, according to details of an 8.9 trillion yen ($55.6 bn) budget request for the coming fiscal year that is only a small increase from this year's 8.8 trillion yen request. Under its five-year defence strategy set in 2022, Japan has doubled its defence spending to about 2% of its gross domestic product, with further details to come after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government approves a new security and defence strategy aimed at strengthening Japan's counterstrike capability.

items.headline: NASA launches space telescope
items.gist: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope successfully lifted off aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Kennedy Space Centre on Sunday and separated from the upper stage about 30 minutes later, beginning a 100-day journey to the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point. Equipped with a 2.4-metre primary mirror and 300.8-megapixel Wide Field Instrument with a field of view 100 times larger than Hubble's, Roman could discover up to 100,000 exoplanets during its five-year mission.

Brussels also designated the Reddit forum and the popular gaming network Roblox as "very large" online platforms, a label that comes with additional obligations and oversight.

items.headline: AstroRad vest offers lighter shield against solar storms
items.gist: StemRad, with Lockheed Martin, developed the AstroRad vest using hydrogen-rich polymers to shield bone marrow and organs; NASA tested it on the ISS in 2019–2020 and on Artemis I in 2022 with dummies Helga and Zohar. items.headline: A Welcome Change (Opinion)
items.gist: Richard Lloyd writes that the RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's call for oneness during his US tour should be welcomed if it represents a real change of heart for an organisation known for ideology propounding exclusion of religious minorities, citing Bhagwat's New York declaration that "if a Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslims in Bharat, he will not remain a Hindu." Lloyd argues critics would be justified in terming it hypocrisy if meant only for US audiences, noting Muslims and Christians have found public space shrinking since 2019, while Pakistan's coalition government has taken small steps toward reconciliation by restoring Hindu names in Lahore.

items.headline: Modi in quest for an Eurasian highway (Opinion)
items.gist: Meenakashi Lekhi writes that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's four-day Central Asia visit—including bilateral talks in Uzbekistan and the 26th SCO summit in Bishkek—is important because Central Asia is a gateway to Europe and India needs resilient multi-modal connectivity after geopolitical disruptions in Hormuz and Chabahar compromised traditional Middle East routes. She argues India must build genuine strategic interdependence through trade, technology, healthcare, critical minerals and digital infrastructure, and that Modi's SCO participation aims to create connectivity that cannot be held hostage to another country's geopolitical crisis.

items.headline: Rebuilding for future floods (Opinion)
items.gist: Writing after the August 26 catastrophic flood along Nepal's Lende-Bhote Koshi system that killed more than 900 people and left over 4,000 missing, retired Geological Survey of India Additional Director General N R Ramesh argues the disaster exposes the Himalayan region's geological fragility and the need for flood-hazard zoning, slope stabilisation and early-warning systems rather than rebuilding alone. He notes India faces downstream risk from barrier lakes on the Tibetan side and from upstream Chinese infrastructure, citing bodies recovered in Uttar Pradesh and concerns over information control and river-flow manipulation near the international boundary.

items.headline: When policy turns, explanation must follow (Opinion)
items.gist: Economist Ajit Ranade uses the Reserve Bank of India's abrupt decision to advance the closing date of the FCNR(B) deposit scheme from September 30 to August 31 — nine days after Governor Sanjay Malhotra said there was no proposal to close it early — to argue that evidence-backed policy reversals are defensible but unexplained U-turns erode institutional credibility. He contends policymakers should pre-specify triggers for course changes and explain what changed on the ground, citing parallels from farm reforms, PLI, IMF programmes and World Bank shifts.

items.headline: The missing urgency in due process (Opinion)
items.gist: The piece examines Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta's three letters to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant in August accusing Rajasthan Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma of corruption, nepotism and roster misuse, and urging immediate transfer of a chief justice from another high court. items.headline: Cloud seeding demands grounded goals (Opinion)
items.gist: The editorial cautions that Karnataka's Rs 28.52-crore cloud-seeding programme — 200 flight hours over 60 days across four revenue divisions amid below-normal monsoon — must keep realistic expectations, noting past experiments in 2003, 2017 and 2019-20 and US estimates of zero to 20% added precipitation. It says seeding can supplement agriculture when moisture-laden clouds exist but cannot substitute watershed development, groundwater recharge, efficient irrigation and drought-resilient farming.

He draws parallels to the current war in Iran, where Donald Trump has hinted at quitting before reversing course, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth promised a swift campaign unlike Afghanistan, and military leaders now describe a blockade that may last months or indefinitely.

items.headline: A woman's clothes and cultural loyalty (Opinion)

She contends moral condemnation settled on the actress rather than the brand, that Raksha Bandhan does not prescribe a dress code, and that digitally organised outrage compels corporate withdrawal and greater creative timidity around festivals.

items.headline: Trees felled in one swoop (Opinion)
items.gist: Vandit Jain of Chandigarh writes that large-scale tree felling for roads, highways and buildings contributes to rising temperatures, air pollution, soil erosion and habitat loss, and that authorities should minimise tree loss and replace trees through plantation drives.

items.headline: The battle within the BJP in Bengal (Opinion)
items.gist: Sayantan Ghosh writes that 100 days after Suvendu Adhikari became West Bengal’s first BJP Chief Minister, a contest is unfolding among the RSS, State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya, and Mr. Adhikari over whether the party will dismantle or inherit Trinamool networks.

Adhikari over whether the party will dismantle or inherit Trinamool networks.
The party has expelled more than 30 leaders and suspended around 250 over allegations of corruption, extortion and anti-party activity.
three former Trinamool Rajya Sabha members have joined the BJP.
Around 20 rebel Trinamool MPs have merged with the Nationalist Citizen Party of India, which seeks a merger with the BJP.

items.headline: The need for political unity in Kashmir (Opinion)
items.gist: Anando Bhakto writes that after Omar Abdullah came to power in October 2024, July protests in Delhi by Abdullah, Mehbooba Mufti and Srinagar MP Ruhullah Mehdi illustrated divisions in Kashmiri leadership over restoring federal guarantees after the August 5, 2019 changes. He argues Gupkar politicians need political unity, that the Lieutenant Governor still wields significant power, and that after the April 2025 Baisaran terrorist attack the houses of at least 10 alleged militants were razed, including that of Aadil Thoker at Guri Thukarpora in Anantnag.

items.headline: Discipline in classrooms, a collective pursuit (Opinion)
items.gist: Anantha Padmanabhan argues that recent disruptive incidents in Tamil Nadu schools should be viewed in perspective rather than as proof of a generation losing its way, calling for sensible digital-use policies, teacher training in adolescent development and conflict resolution, access to counsellors, and constructive parental engagement. Discipline must remain proportionate and transparent, with policymakers resisting both complacency and alarmism while collecting better data on bullying, violence and student well-being so interventions are evidence-based rather than driven by isolated headlines.

items.headline: We must reform higher education by empowering educators (Opinion)
items.gist: Anitha Ramachander writes that achieving Viksit Bharat 2047 requires sweeping change in higher education led by educators, noting that many institutions do not pay teachers fairly, increase workloads, and force faculty into transactional mentoring while burdening them with accreditation paperwork. She calls for hiring passionate talent, reducing teaching loads to allow reflection and innovation, genuine research support, revising PhD frameworks, fair pay with clear career pathways, and promoting work-life balance so faculty can inspire students rather than merely meet obligations.

items.headline: Five mindsets that will set your career trajectory (Opinion)
items.gist: Anubha Khandelwal warns that many fresh graduates enter the workforce with mindset traps — the "not my job" trap, treating feedback as a personal attack, viewing success as a fixed algorithm, fearing embarrassment over asking questions, and chasing strategy roles without ground experience — that can stall careers before they begin. Citing the 70-20-10 Learning Model, she argues the first 24 months should be an investment phase to build career capital through on-the-job execution, absorbing feedback, and embracing imperfect workplaces rather than seeking a flawless first job.

items.headline: Tirukkural and the Gita (Opinion)
items.gist: In a Faith column, Thaneerpalli Krishnan Swamy said Tirukkural, honoured as the “Ulaga Podhu Marai,” teaches aram, porul, inbam and veedu, and that its teachings parallel the Bhagavad Gita on dharma, karma, spiritual wisdom and liberation.

items.headline: Leo’s glorious position in football is set in stone (Opinion)
items.gist: K.C. Vijaya Kumar writes that Lionel Messi’s international retirement leaves him in football’s pantheon with Pelé and Diego Maradona after he won the World Cup at Doha in 2022, the prize Maradona last secured in 1986, and after Spain denied an encore in this year’s final.

items.headline: The broken promise of right to work (Opinion)
items.gist: Rajendran Narayanan and Vijay Ram S. write that replacing MGNREGA with the VB-GRAM G Act, implemented from July 1, weakened the rural right-to-work framework; about 3.44 crore households worked about 44 crore person-days under MGNREGA in July–August on average over five years, with a 68% decrease this year.
